title: Programming Languages and Frameworks
answer: The languages AI is written in and the frameworks built on top of them, tracked by adoption, releases, licence, and integrations.

reading.body:
The software layer of AI splits into three groups, and the smallest of them is the languages themselves.

Programming languages carry 7 entries, AI frameworks 17, and inference engines 12. The frameworks and serving layers together hold more than four times the tracked items of the languages they are built on. That ratio is the useful signal: the work of running and wiring models has outgrown the work of writing the code that defines them.

For AI specifically, this matters because inference engines are where compute meets software. vLLM, TensorRT, and llama.cpp sit between a model and the hardware that serves it, and that is the layer where throughput, memory, and cost per token are actually decided. A field with 12 tracked serving projects against 7 languages is a field optimizing deployment, not invention.

The data does not say which projects are winning, how adoption is measured, or what the counts include. It records that these categories are tracked and how many items fall in each, nothing about releases, licences, or integrations despite the summary naming them. Treat the counts as a map of where attention sits, not as evidence about performance or maturity.
